correctness.rationale: Unique path to the sole caster forces all directed approvals to parent edges. Conditional subtrees are independent given the parent time; induction proves the F_v and H_c maxima and the sum of root-child optima. A sweep of inclusive trust intervals with a max-heap proves the O(M+nL log(L+1)) bound and supports exact reconstruction. The explicit four-voter zero-horizon instance is individually feasible but synchronously impossible, and the two rooted-tree shapes on at most three voters exclude smaller obstructions. Independent exact brute-force enumeration agrees with reconstructed optimizer on 3,900 varied finite instances. No finite experiment substitutes for the arbitrary-size proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is restricted to date-synchronized, one-caster rooted forests with arbitrary voter- and time-dependent trust windows. The 2023 motivating source develops the temporal and confluence notions and general hardness/retrospective-trust methods, but none of its inspected theorems establishes this forest recurrence, near-linear-in-expanded-input complexity or the sharp four-voter obstruction. Full-text comparison with 2019 static-tree guru games, 2019 single-path waiting-time algorithms and 2023 temporal group-Steiner optimization found different objects or objectives, not a broader implication. Repeated targeted mathematical-record searches had no directly comparable claim; an unindexed special case or a subsequent revised version remains a risk, explicitly delimited.
residual_risks: A more general yet unindexed temporal-forest algorithm with bounded waiting could subsume the result without mentioning liquid democracy.
The 2024 conference version of the motivating preprint has not been read in full and may add restrictions or algorithms.
The timestamp-synchronized action requirement is stricter than interpreting every path timestamp independently; priority and scope statements are restricted accordingly.

value.rationale: The source motivates the central tension between temporal feasibility, confluence and utility. The result identifies a natural acyclic network regime in which arbitrary non-retrospective trust profiles still permit almost input-linear exact welfare optimization; its sharp four-voter example establishes a genuine global coherence obstruction despite individually valid routes and final-round approvals. This is a useful structural boundary for a multi-voter decision mechanism rather than a mere implementation speedup or an arbitrary finite census.
